vector.direction: A black screen with one glowing world on it: thin pale coastlines with a soft halo, land as faint fills, a dim wide-tracked PUSHING lying in the strait the Federation is crossing, and the danger painted so it reads from across the room: amber hatching sweeping down the eastern shore, Driftholm a pulsing red knot, your three promises in crisp white with WE DEFEND, and a white target reticle breathing on Lintel. Colour means one thing each (cyan is the Federation and its treaty bar, white is you, amber is pressure, red is fighting, grey is the world and its chrome), and the only chrome is two thin lines at the top, one ticker line at the bottom, and two small readouts in the corners; the call is a vector panel hung from the reticle by a leader line, with a line-drawn General Halder, his forty words, three advisers in character, and three outlined buttons of which only BACK IT glows white.
vector.hero: The eastern shore of the Sound: the amber-hatched block of Kelpmouth, Brackwater and Lintel with the white reticle pulsing on Lintel and "LINTEL · TESTED" under it, two cyan brigade markers sitting on the Lintel line, and the cyan chevrons sweeping down out of the Federation above it. On the call screen the hero is the reticle hanging just above the panel, tied to General Halder's face by a single white line.
vector.watcher: "The blue lot up top are pushing down into that strait and they've taken the red island; she's drawn white rings round the places she swore to defend, and now they've parked tanks on one of them, the one with the crosshairs, to see if she meant it; the red line at the top is the war and the blue one is how close they are to signing."
vector.notes: What is in the files: the map is re-projected (0.97 wide, 1.14 tall, straits widened by bloc offsets) but keeps all 30 regions, names, joins and lanes; the six islands are redrawn as seeded irregular coasts instead of circles; coasts are computed as the edges not shared between two regions, so the outer coast glows while internal borders stay thin and dim; sea lanes and island joins are trimmed to the water. Everything animates with SMIL inside the SVG (reticle pulse, Driftholm breathing, chevron trails flowing, the ticker scrolling, the incoming-call ring), so there is no script and no @keyframes; the frames are complete with animation off. Fonts could not be fetched through this container's proxy, so both screenshots are the fallback stack (Liberation Sans / Liberation Mono); Barlow Condensed is narrower than the fallback, so labels only gain room when it loads. Next with a budget: (1) a 10-second motion pass: chevrons that actually travel the lane, the reticle tightening when the call comes, the ticker catching light when a headline mentions a promised place; (2) a true coastline redraw at 2x detail with a feTurbulence shimmer on the sea and a faint sweep so the black is never flat; (3) a tap-and-hold region card that shows the WE DEFEND cost before you promise, using the same white outline language; (4) the full adviser cast as line portraits (Dove, Intel) so the call can show who is talking, and a second call layout for when two advisers disagree; (5) a real on-device check of label sizes at 7.4 px on a 390-wide phone, bumping to 8 px and staggering island labels if any reader struggles; (6) a sound sketch (one low WOPR tone per ladder step) because this look wants to be heard.

paper.direction: A paper situation map under a desk lamp: ink coastlines with water-lining and hachured hills on warm grained paper, bloc washes hand-tinted, names set like a printed sheet, and on top of it the marks of a person losing sleep — black grease-pencil rings for the promises with a scrawled WE DEFEND, red pencil hatching where the Federation leans, a red wash and FIGHTING stamp on Driftholm, red pushpins with a pencil arrow for the columns on the move, and Lintel over-circled in hard red pencil with TESTED underlined; the two bars are pencil hatching on an index card paper-clipped to the map's corner, the ladder word is a red rubber stamp, the news is a strip of teleprinter tape. The call is the clock stopped on a dark flip-tag at 03:14, a bakelite handset lying off the hook across the map with its coiled cord trailing off the desk, General Halder's words typed on a clipped card, three torn adviser slips, and the three choices as typed forms with a pencil underline and a handwritten 1, 2, 3.
paper.hero: On the day frame it is the map, and within it Lintel: the black promise ring with a second, pressed-hard red ring around it, the printed name underlined in red and the handwritten TESTED beneath, sitting in the lamp's pool between the red-hatched Sound, the pin at Kellmark, and the fleet counter at Lantern Key. On the call frame it is the handset lying across the lit map with the red ring still visible beside it and General Halder's typed card beneath.
paper.watcher: "The red pins up top are the Federation coming down; she's drawn circles round the places she promised to defend, and the one they've gone for is Lintel — it's circled in red and says TESTED. The card says they're PUSHING, one bit of the map is on fire, and the blue pencil bar, 22%, is how close they are to agreeing to stop."
paper.notes: Self-check: rendered four times with Playwright (chromium-1194, 390x844, DPR 2) and iterated on what I saw: round 1 had Kelpmouth/Brackwater colliding, Northwake hidden under the calendar, two WE DEFENDs and THE SOUND clipped at the frame edges, the handset and tape overhanging the frame, and a muddy sheet; round 2 fixed those and found WE DEFEND at Lintel running into THE SOUND and the Farsouth labels peeking between the caller card and the slips; round 3 fixed those and the fallback render exposed the calendar's "next call: day 21" wrapping without Caveat and the call tape overflowing the bottom; round 4 is clean in both font modes with a DOM bounding-box check reporting nothing outside the frame. Fonts: Google Fonts CSS is blocked for Chromium here (proxy CA), so I fetched the woff2 files with curl and loaded them only in my preview wrapper; the deliverables have no @font-face and were also rendered with system fallbacks (Liberation Mono for the typewriter, DejaVu Serif for the handwriting) and hold up. Colour has three meanings only: red is the Federation (pins, hatching, wash, the test ring, the stamp), black graphite is your hand (promise rings, fleet counter, arrows annotated in pencil), blue is the treaty bar and the Republic's flag. Builder is parametric (build.py reads geo.json, the same 30 regions, names and joins; the six sea discs are redrawn as seeded irregular islands; the map is stretched 1.08 vertically and the call frame is the same map shifted so Lintel sits under the lamp). With a budget, next: (1) a real lamp — a visible brass shade at the top edge, a warm cast with a hard-edged pool and a second cold fill from a window, and the vignette breathing slightly over the day clock; (2) replace the CSS/SVG paper with a photographed paper texture and a printed-map halftone, and give the coast its proper hachure (short strokes computed perpendicular to the coastline) rather than the clipped shading used here; (3) motion — the pushpins drop in with a shadow, the pencil arrow draws itself, the grease ring is scribbled on when you promise, the stamp slams when the ladder word changes, the tape feeds one line at a time with a teleprinter chatter and the handset rattles on the desk when the call comes; (4) a second pass on the counters: proper wargame chits with a strength number for the Federation's brigades and a ship silhouette for the fleet, plus a legend card tucked under the map edge; (5) unique island coastlines drawn by hand instead of seeded noise, and bloc names set on arcs; (6) an ink-bleed and a torn corner on the tape, finger smudges on the grease pencil, and a sound bed (clock, teleprinter, the lamp's hum) tested with the over-the-shoulder reader.

cards.direction: A hand-drawn paper map (parchment grain, inked coasts, wave-hatched sea, mountains and pines) sits quietly under a deck of dark playing cards, with the pending test poking up from the bottom as "THE PHONE · LINTEL"; colour means only five things: iron grey is the Federation, green is the Republic, red is fighting, amber is under pressure, blue is the treaty. At 03:14 the map goes dark and one Reigns-style card fills the screen: a flat-vector portrait of General Ruun Halder lit from one side, his 22-word message in a warm serif, his line as a red pull-quote, the Dove and the Intel Director as small face chips, and three big choice cards (swipe left to BACK DOWN, hold to WAIT, swipe right to BACK IT) in the same three colours as the map.
cards.hero: On the call screen the hero is Halder's face: a 334 x 250 flat-vector portrait (close-cropped grey hair, heavy brows, scar, stubbled jaw, invented chevron collar pins, warm key light from the left with a hard shadow side) on a cream card that fills 57% of the screen. On the day-18 screen the hero is the map itself: a parchment sheet in a neatline, the red hand-drawn ring around Lintel with the green WE DEFEND seal inside it, Driftholm burning under a smoke plume, and two iron arrows of Federation armour moving.
cards.watcher: "The grey country up top is marching on her, and they've set that island on fire; she stamped a green seal on three places she swore to defend and now they've drawn a red ring round one of them; that old general is telling her to send the brigade, and the blue bar is how close the other side is to agreeing to stop."
cards.notes: The map leans PAPER (parchment grain via feTurbulence, inked dashed borders, coastal hachure, wave pattern on the sea, hand-drawn glyphs); pair it with the paper direction, not the vector one. Both files are generated by build.py from geo.json (same 30 regions, names and joins; the six island discs are redrawn as six distinct blob coastlines of the same centres and radii). Self-check: rendered with Playwright at 390x844 @2x, three iteration passes (row-two collision, arrow through the THE CAP watermark, hidden compass, clipped chips, BACK DOWN wrapping, DAY 18 colliding with the clock glyphs under the real Fraunces); an element-bounds check reports nothing outside the frame; also rendered with no web fonts (Charter/Liberation fallback) and with upright-only weights, since assemble.py's font link requests no italics, so the italics in the assembled page will be synthesized obliques: acceptable, but if you want true italics, add ital axes to the link. shot.js needs its fontcache (deleted to keep the folder small); run it with the fonts flag 0 for a fallback render. Words beyond MOMENT.md are only chrome labels: WIRE, THEY ARE, the key, "swipe left / hold / swipe right", "the Dove", "observations only", "rings day 21". With a budget, next: (1) commission or hand-draw a real portrait set in this flat two-tone style (Halder, the Dove, the Intel Director, plus 3 or 4 more callers) with two expressions each, so the call card can change face with the ladder word; (2) animate the call: the card slides up from the deck with the phone-ring arcs pulsing, dragging the big card left/right tilts it and previews the choice's cost line (Reigns feel), WAIT is a press-and-hold with an hourglass fill; (3) the map: replace the procedural grain with a painted parchment texture, give each bloc one or two unique landmarks (Wintermast's fortress, Edda Vale's lantern tower, the Lintel bridge) so regions are recognisable without reading, and make the Federation arrows and the Lintel ring the only things that move on the still screen (slow dash crawl, ring breathing); (4) a second night mode of the map for the call background where the Lintel ring glows through the dark; (5) type: license Fraunces' SOFT/WONK axes (or self-host) so the stamp and the clock can use the wonky optical style, and load true Alegreya italics.
